chapter: Hampton, New York and Lee's own band
title: Forming his own band at Billy Berg's as Lester arrives
summary: After Hamp, Lee formed a band with Red Callender and Bumps Myers at Billy Berg's, and the union moved to restrict Lester's playing when he came out.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: But he was a nice man -- very, very nice man. And he looked out for me. Just as I told you like Ethel Waters did? Looked out for me, you know. I lived where he and Gladys lived ... always. So that's just growing pains, I guess, but after Hamp, oh yes -- after Hamp, I came back home, and I formed a band with Red Callender, Bumps Myers, Paul Campbell Gamel was trumpet -- Louis Gonzales on guitar. And Arthur Twine was playing piano.

And we used to rehearse 5 days a week, and then Lester quit Basie, and we were working at a place called Billy Billie Berg's, but, see, Billy Berg's had 4 or 5 places in Los Angeles, and in '42, Billy Bergs was at La Cienega and Pico, where the bank is now; where the movie house is, at La Cienega and Pico; that's where Billy Berg's was. And ...

Oh yeah, it was called Billy Berg's. That's what he called all of his clubs. But a funny thing happened. Lester came out. Now, I told you -- or I stated earlier that we had separate locals, so everybody imagined, because Lester was my brother, when he came out, he was gonna

join the band, that I was gonna get rid of Bumps Myers. Well, now, Bumps was really, you know -- everybody in L.A. loved Bumps, you know, big smile, infectious smile -- and he was a big guy, but really, just like a little chubby bear or something. But a nice man. But I had no intention of axing Bumps. What I ended up doing was having 2 tenors, one trumpet and a guitar, you know, which is a real big sound that people didn't believe.
But we had a lot of arrangements made for them, and we used to rehearse 6 days a week, I think it was, and we would learn one arrangement per day, you know?
It's awful close to the end of the tape.
Yeah. And what they made Lester do -- what the Union made Lester do -- they said that he could not play with us; that all he could do ...
